leads.oddeven: Even transits are deeper. SPOC SAP: odd 9566, even 10086 ppm, difference -520 ppm (5.2% of the depth). Significance: permutation 4.6 sigma (p=5e-5 from 20000 relabelings), bootstrap 5.1, scatter-based 5.0, paired adjacent transits -489+-104 ppm (4.7). PDCSAP gives the same: -527 ppm, 4.6 sigma. Template-free central-box variants give -330 to -494 ppm (3.5-4.2 sigma). Separate batman fits to the odd and even folds give 9737 vs 10248 ppm. Per SPOC sector: S27 -437 (2.4 sigma), S67 -689 (3.0), S68 -443 (2.6). QLP has the same sign in all 8 sectors: S27 -401, S67 -500, S68 -570, S94 -198, S95 -426, S101 -211, S102 -315, S104 -76 ppm. The QLP-only sectors S94-S104, independent of the SPOC photons, give paired -247+-65 ppm (3.8 sigma). Combined significance is about 6 sigma. Pseudo-parity groupings give <=2.1 sigma. Identical code on the controls gives <=1.5 sigma, and a 5% odd/even difference injected into LHS 3844b was recovered without bias.
leads.secondary: Our pipeline's 74-sigma 'secondary' at 2P=0.7808 d is just the alternate eclipse, at phase 0.5000, with 95% of the primary depth. Occultation test at phase 0.5 of 0.39 d: SPOC PDCSAP -39+-48 ppm, QLP -48+-24 ppm. Both are consistent with zero once the expected -30 to -50 ppm bias from phase-curve curvature is allowed for. An undiluted irradiated giant planet with k>=0.1 at a/R*~1.7-1.8 (T_eq>=3000 K) should give >~600 ppm. The phase scan from 0.3 to 0.7 shows no dip above ~130 ppm; the narrow window limits the range. SPOC DV weak-secondary maximum MES is 3.5, i.e. no secondary. Out-of-eclipse harmonics at 0.7808 d: cos(4 pi phi) = -100+-26 ppm (SPOC) and -106+-22 ppm (QLP), minima at the eclipses, ellipsoidal-like. The cos(2 pi phi) and sin(2 pi phi) terms are consistent with zero.
leads.summary: Probably an eclipsing binary with near-equal eclipses at P=0.7807705 d, twice the CTOI period, rather than a 0.39-d hot Jupiter. Three independent lines of evidence: (1) odd/even depths differ by 5%, at 4.6-5 sigma in SPOC alone, replicated at 3.8 sigma in independent QLP sectors, with the same sign in 8 of 8 sectors; (2) no occultation, below ~100 ppm where a planet would need >~600 ppm; (3) ~100 ppm ellipsoidal-like modulation. Supporting points: the shape is V/grazing (k>0.25 preferred), and a Jupiter-sized body at P=9.4 h would be inside the Roche limit unless rho_p>~1.8 g/cc. The source lies within a few arcsec of the target. Difference images and DV ditco (1.0-1.9+-2.6 arcsec) reject the 33-arcsec G=17 neighbour, and no resolved Gaia star is bright enough. However, Gaia's constant RV and small vbroad, plus the low ellipsoidal amplitude, argue against the bright F star itself being a 0.78-d twin EB. Most likely the eclipses come from a faint, unresolved near-equal-mass EB (RUWE 2.16), as a hierarchical triple or blend. Caveat: the SPOC DV multi-sector odd/even fit shows nothing; its per-sector fits agree in sign. Suggested ExoFOP note: 'likely EB at 0.7808 d (odd/even 5%, no occultation), host star not determined'. Do not say 'EB on target'.

leads.secondary: Strong secondary eclipse at phase 0.4985+-0.001 (fitted), the highest peak of the full-phase scan. Box depth 1144 ppm (8.5 sigma against the fake-phase null, TESS-SPOC SAP), 1162 ppm (9.6, PDCSAP), 1046 ppm (12.5, QLP). A trapezoid fit gives 1270-1310 ppm and ~5-6 h duration. Secondary/primary ratio is 0.28-0.30, against 0.27 in the Gaia G band. Gaia's two-Gaussian model puts the secondary at phase 0.5036; that fit has reduced chi2 of 14, so the 0.005 phase difference is probably model systematics. A ~1.2 ppt occultation is impossible for a 5.5 R_E planet (expected <~50 ppm). Our pipeline's 6.8-sigma secondary is confirmed.
leads.summary: Nearby-EB blend. The signal is the Gaia DR3 / VSX eclipsing binary Gaia DR3 4982105786405613952, 23 arcsec ESE, leaking into the aperture. It matches in period (0.6 sigma), primary epoch (6.6 min after 656 cycles), secondary phase (~0.5) and secondary/primary depth ratio (0.28 vs 0.27). Difference imaging in all 7 sectors puts the PSF-fitted source 0.04-0.25 px from the EB and 1.0-1.2 px (21-25 arcsec) from the target, with position errors 0.02-0.1 px. The neighbour-only model beats target-only by delta-chi2 125-1760 in every sector, and the implied eclipse depth on the EB is 19-23% (Gaia: 30%). The neighbour is 4.27 mag fainter in T, so it needs only ~20% intrinsic depth (<100%). The transit-derived stellar density, 0.05 g/cc, is 25x below the G-dwarf target's 1.27 g/cc: the 4.35-h V-shaped event is far too long for the target. The depth also varies by sector and aperture (QLP 2.7-4.8 ppt), as expected for an off-target source. Suggested ExoFOP note: 'NEB: signal from Gaia DR3 4982105786405613952 (23 arcsec, P=4.39254 d EB)'.

leads.summary: An eclipsing binary at P=2.1516 d (twice the CTOI period) with eclipses differing by 12%; detected at 7-22 sigma depending on the estimator and seen in all 9 independent sectors. Supporting this, the out-of-eclipse light curve shows 2-5.5 ppt modulation at P~2.10-2.15 d in 7 of 9 sectors, consistent with spots on a component rotating in step with a 2.15-d orbit. The eclipses come from the target or an unresolved companion within ~1 arcsec. Evidence: the difference-image centroid is within 0.1-1.3 arcsec (+-0.6-1.1) of the out-of-eclipse centroid. The 4.8-arcsec, 4.6-mag-fainter neighbour (G=17.1, likely bound) would need >100% eclipses and is disfavoured by delta-chi2 450-1060. Gaia's smooth ~20 km/s RV trend argues against the bright star being a 2.15-d near-twin SB2 (K~100 km/s expected). Together with RUWE 4.9, a hierarchical triple with the EB as the companion is most likely. Either way it is not a planet. Suggested ExoFOP note: 'EB at P=2.1516 d (alternating depths 16.5/14.5 ppt in all sectors); CTOI epoch is off by 0.31 phase'.

leads.summary: A blend, but of a planet, not an EB: the CTOI is WASP-94 A b (TOI-107.01) seen in WASP-94 B's aperture. Host established three ways. (1) SPOC DV difference-image centroid sits 14.4+-2.6 arcsec (multi-sector) and 14.7+-2.5 arcsec (S68) from B's catalogue position, i.e. on A; for A the offsets are 0.8 and 0.4 arcsec. (2) Our difference-image scene fits in S68 and S95 put the source on A (0.003-0.13 px) and prefer an A-only model by delta-chi2 ~2000-2800. (3) The PDCSAP depth on A is constant at 12.80-12.89 ppt over 5 sectors, while on B it wanders from 12.5 to 15.0 ppt, the signature of a contaminating signal being crowding-corrected. Our pipeline's odd/even EB flag was spurious for both stars. Already documented on ExoFOP and in DTARPS II; nothing new.

controls:
I ran the identical battery on five confirmed or known planets observed in or next to S104/S105, using the same products (SPOC 2-min SAP/PDCSAP, TESS-SPOC, QLP SAP_FLUX), the same per-event local polynomial baselines and the same calibrations. Calibrations used: parity-permutation and bootstrap for odd/even, paired adjacent transits, and fake-phase null distributions for secondaries.
(1) LHS 3844 b (TOI-136.01, confirmed; P=0.463 d, 4600 ppm, T=11.92; SPOC S1-S104, 11 sectors, 507 transits; control for the 0.39-d lead). Odd/even -29 ppm (-0.3 sigma permutation); paired +8+-101 ppm (0.1 sigma); per sector <=2.1 sigma with mixed signs. Secondary at phase 0.5: -31+-48 ppm (-0.5 sigma). The 2P pipeline flag (sec 19 sigma at 0.926 d) has the same period-doubling cause as 327712163's 74-sigma 'secondary'. A 5% odd/even difference injected into it was recovered at -257 ppm (expected -230).
(2) WASP-4 b (TOI-232.01, KP; P=1.338 d, 27.1 ppt, T=11.83; SPOC 8 sectors incl. S103/S105/S106). Odd/even +59 ppm (0.6 sigma); paired 0.5 sigma; TESS-SPOC 0.1 sigma; QLP 0.2 sigma. Secondary +168 ppm at phase 0.505 (3.1 sigma).
(3) WASP-5 b (TOI-250.01, KP; P=1.628 d, 13.9 ppt, T=11.55; SPOC 7 sectors incl. S103/S105/S106). Odd/even 0.7 sigma (paired 1.1); our original pipeline had flagged it at 4.4 sigma. Secondary +166 ppm (3.3 sigma).
(4) HATS-68 b (TOI-117.01, KP; P=3.586 d, 5.7 ppt, T=11.78; SPOC 9 sectors incl. S104/S105). Odd/even 0.0 sigma; the pipeline had flagged 5.4 sigma. Secondary -26 ppm (-0.3 sigma); scan maximum 3.1-4.1 sigma with 19 effective trial phases.
(5) WASP-94 A b (TOI-107.01, KP; P=3.950 d, 12.8 ppt, T=9.64; SPOC 5 sectors incl. S95/S105). Odd/even 0.4 sigma PDCSAP, 1.5 sigma SAP; the pipeline had flagged 16.4 sigma. Secondary +99 ppm (3.7 sigma SAP).
Conclusions from the controls:
- Calibrated odd/even on real planets is <=1.5 sigma in every product, so the five pipeline odd/even flags were artifacts of white-noise errors.
- Calibrated phase-0.5 'secondaries' in planets reach 3-3.7 sigma at 100-170 ppm (real occultations or systematics). I therefore treat a secondary as EB evidence only if it is >5 sigma and too deep for a planetary occultation.
- QLP SAP_FLUX depths are 10-35% shallower than SPOC PDCSAP for the controls, so QLP depths were used only for relative tests.
- The leads judged strong (327712163: about 6 sigma odd/even combined, 8 of 8 sectors same sign; 206599822: 7-22 sigma, 9 of 9 sectors; 102064145: secondary 8.5-12.5 sigma at 28% of the primary depth plus pixel-level localisation) are well outside the control distribution.

leads.data_used: Sectors 1, 28, 68, 95 and 105: QLP SAP_FLUX for all five, and TESS-SPOC SAP and PDCSAP for S1, S28 and S68. I also did my own 3x3-pixel photometry on TESScut cutouts for S105 and S106 (S106 is outside our search). Each transit was measured with a local quadratic baseline plus a fixed-shape transit template. Gaia DR3 was used for RVs, IPD flags and neighbours. Ephemeris check: per-event timing gives P = 0.65183559 +- 0.00000016 d, and a joint BLS gives 0.651834-0.651835. RAVEN's period (0.65183695 +- 0.00000057) is slightly too long, so its ephemeris is about 7 min off by S105. That offset is small next to the 1.5 h duration and does not cause the odd/even effect. The odd/even labels stay coherent across all eight years.
leads.oddeven: Even-numbered events (relative to T0 = BTJD 3165.6697) are about twice as deep as odd ones in every sector and every product. QLP SAP, all sectors: odd 2460+-71, even 5372+-132 ppm. That is 19.4 sigma with errors scaled to the per-transit scatter. In the permutation test, no shuffle of the odd/even labels within a sector came close, out of 4000 (z_perm 10.5, p < 2.5e-4). Bootstrap over transits gives 18.5 sigma. The null test at fake phases has a spread of 48 ppm, which puts the observed difference at about 60 sigma. Per sector (QLP, odd/even ppm): S1 2648/5811, S28 2763/6450, S68 2730/6041, S95 2548/5126, S105 2102/4317; single-sector significance is 9 to 13 sigma (z_perm 4.3 to 5.4). TESS-SPOC PDCSAP: 2772+-85 vs 6004+-103 ppm (24 sigma), with S1/S28/S68 at 2667/6210, 2866/6107 and 2794/5764. My TESScut photometry: S105 3020/5936 and S106 2869/5622 (18 sigma combined). The per-event depths form two cleanly separated groups of 149 events. Folding the odd and even events separately gives model depths of 2430 and 5490 ppm, with the same duration (1.55 vs 1.53 h). The odd-minus-even timing offset is about 2 min, consistent with a circular orbit. The true period is therefore 1.3036712 +- 0.0000005 d, with unequal eclipses: primary about 5800-6000 ppm and secondary about 2800 ppm (PDCSAP).
leads.secondary: I masked the transits and measured a box of the transit duration at many phases, calibrated against the phase-scan scatter. At phase 0.5 of 0.6518 d the depth is 42+-45 ppm (0.9 sigma; 0.7 sigma against the scan). The most significant dip anywhere in the phase scan is |z| = 2.0, so there is no further eclipse at any phase. In the 1.3037-d picture, the shallower eclipse is itself the secondary.
leads.other_tests: Depth across sectors and products: QLP gives 3866, 4485, 4405, 3848 and 3140 ppm for S1, S28, S68, S95 and S105; TESS-SPOC PDC gives 4224-4530 ppm; my TESScut photometry gives 4355 ppm. QLP comes out shallower in S95 and later, but the controls show the same 10-28% QLP depth suppression in recent sectors, so this is not evidence of blending. Shape: the best fit is V-shaped and grazing (b ~0.92, a/R* ~2.0). The implied stellar density is 0.36 g/cc against the TIC value of 1.25 g/cc. That is mildly supportive of an EB but degenerate for grazing fits. Host star: Gaia DR3 gives RV error 0.86 km/s from 15 transits and robust RV amplitude 9.9 km/s, which limits the reflex motion to roughly K < 5 km/s. Two eclipses with a depth ratio of about 0.45 need two stars of similar temperature (a K-type companion would give K1 ~100 km/s), so the EB cannot be on the target star. Difference images from TESScut S105 and S106 (all events, and the deep events alone) put the eclipsing source within about 0.2 px (~4") of the target. Fixing the source at the 18" neighbour (T~16.0) is worse by delta-chi2 600-1400, and the 47" and 55" neighbours (T~14.7) are worse by about 1000. All three neighbours would otherwise be bright enough (required eclipse depths about 50% and 14%). Gaia shows ipd_frac_multi_peak = 41% with RUWE 1.03, which suggests a close (<~1") companion. Our S105-only rerun reproduces the pipeline flag: odd 2104+-112 vs even 4298+-135 ppm, 12.5 sigma.
leads.summary: Strong, multiply calibrated evidence that the 0.6518-d signal is an eclipsing binary at P = 1.3036712 d with unequal eclipses (~5900 and ~2800 ppm PDCSAP). The deeper eclipse falls on the same parity in all five sectors from 2018 to 2026, in every product, and in my own S106 photometry, so a wrong period, ephemeris drift, data gaps or a few bad transits cannot explain it. Gaia's flat RVs rule out the EB being on the target star. The difference images place the source within ~4" of the target and rule out the resolved Gaia neighbours, which points to an unresolved bound or background EB. This is not recorded in RAVEN, on ExoFOP, or in any EB catalogue. Suggested ExoFOP note: P_EB = 1.3036712 d, primary T0 = BJD_TDB 2460165.6697.

leads.already_known: ExoFOP lists it as a PC with no TFOPWG disposition, no observing notes, no imaging and no spectroscopy; the only file is the RAVEN PDF. The ExoFOP depth of 17040+-10662 ppm is just (Rp/Rs)^2 from a grazing fit (b = 1.016, Rp/Rs = 0.13); the real dip is about 3000-4400 ppm. RAVEN puts it in the vetted sample with prob_EB 0.993, prob_HEB 0.938 (the lowest score), positional probability 1.0, sector_flag False, no notes, transit S/N 3.97, Rp 21.8 Re, and it was not validated. Gaia DR3 has an SB1 orbit for the target: P = 287.1 d, e = 0.45, K1 = 16.9 km/s, giving a companion of at least ~0.67 Msun; RUWE is 2.14. This is a long-period companion, not the 1.68-d signal. The target is not in any EB catalogue (Kostov+25 table2/3/4, Prsa+22, Gaia EB, VSX, Tey+23, IJspeert+24), and no later paper was found.
leads.data_used: QLP SAP for S1, S28, S68, S95 and S105; TESS-SPOC SAP and PDCSAP for S1, S28 and S68; my own TESScut 3x3 photometry for S105 and S106. Ephemeris check: the catalogue ephemeris is stale. Fitting all sectors together gives P = 1.684997 +- ~0.00001 d (QLP per-event 1.6849965, joint BLS 1.684994-1.684997), against RAVEN's 1.6849422 +- 0.0000028. RAVEN's ephemeris therefore predicts the S105 eclipses about 1.8-2.2 h early (S68 about 1.2 h, S95 about 2.0 h), which is about one full duration. A linear ephemeris still leaves sector residuals of 10-25 min. QLP and TESS-SPOC disagree on those residuals for the same sectors, so I treat them as timing noise rather than real timing variations.
leads.oddeven: Odd events (relative to T0 = BTJD 3166.2595) are much deeper than even ones in every sector and product. QLP SAP, all sectors: odd 5523+-126, even 2399+-136 ppm. That is 16.8 sigma with scatter-calibrated errors; the permutation test gives z = 6.8 with p < 2.5e-4, and the bootstrap gives 14.9 sigma. The fake-phase null has a spread of 139 ppm, which puts the difference at 22.5 sigma. Per sector (QLP, odd/even ppm): S1 4637/1488, S28 5361/3103, S68 6164/2965, S95 5498/2258, S105 5447/2142; single-sector significance is 4.8 to 10.9 sigma, and the permutation p-value is at its minimum for about 11 events. TESS-SPOC PDCSAP: 5245+-176 vs 2308+-215 ppm (10.6 sigma), with S1/S28/S68 at 4231/1308, 4936/2624 and 5951/2896. My TESScut photometry: S105 6077/2220 and S106 5750/2541 (15 sigma). The per-event depths form two separated groups. The deep and shallow eclipses are also offset in time by about 20-23 min (QLP) or 20 min (TESS-SPOC) from exactly half a period apart, which suggests a slightly eccentric orbit (e cos w ~0.007). The true period is P_EB = 3.369994 d, with eclipses of about 5200-6200 and 2300-2900 ppm.
leads.secondary: With transits masked, phase 0.5 of 1.685 d gives -36+-52 ppm (-0.7 sigma). The full phase scan has no dip beyond |z| = 1.8, so there is no other eclipse at any phase. The shallow alternate eclipse is the EB's secondary.
leads.other_tests: Depth across sectors and products: QLP 2908-4557 ppm, TESS-SPOC PDC 2649-4410 ppm, my TESScut photometry 4012 ppm. These are consistent within errors, and S1 is low in both products. Shape: V-shaped and grazing (b ~1.26), and the implied density is not meaningful. Duration 2.35-2.5 h against about 3.8 h expected for a central transit. Neighbours and dilution: all Gaia sources within 84" together contribute only 0.28% of the target's flux. The brightest of them (27.5", flux ratio 0.00044) would need an eclipse of more than 1000%, so no resolved neighbour can be the source. Host: the Gaia RV scatter (error 2.88 km/s over 22 transits) is fully explained by the 287-d SB1 orbit. A stellar companion eclipsing the primary every 3.37 d would add K ~50-100 km/s and would have prevented that clean SB1 solution. The most natural explanation is a hierarchical triple (the unseen 287-d companion is itself the 3.37-d EB, matching RAVEN's weakest scenario, HEB), or an unresolved background EB. Our S105-only rerun gives odd 5440+-251 vs even 2110+-177 ppm (10.8 sigma), reproducing the 12.3-sigma pipeline flag.
leads.summary: The 1.685-d CTOI is an eclipsing binary at P_EB = 3.369994 d with unequal eclipses (~5500 vs ~2400 ppm), coherent across five sectors (2018-2026), three independent reductions and my own S106 photometry. The secondary also appears displaced ~20 min from phase 0.5. The target is a known Gaia SB1 (287 d), which together with the absence of resolved contaminants points to a hierarchical-triple or unresolved-companion EB. RAVEN's ephemeris is also stale (eclipses ~2 h later than predicted by 2026). None of this is on ExoFOP or in the RAVEN paper. Suggested note: P_EB = 3.369994 d, deep-eclipse T0 = BJD_TDB 2460167.9433.

leads.already_known: ExoFOP lists it as a PC with no TFOPWG disposition, no notes, no files and no imaging. Bryant & Van Eylen (2025, MNRAS 544, 1186) list it in their Table A1 of new candidates around an early red giant (R* 2.26). Their vetting checked Gaia non-single-star solutions on the target and centroid offsets larger than 1 pixel, and neither would catch a faint eclipsing binary half a pixel away. That binary is already catalogued: Gaia DR3 5952123561802121472 = TIC 218856692 (G = 17.87, T = 17.46, 10.6" from the target) is in Gaia DR3 vari_eclipsing_binary, the Gaia NSS eclipsing-binary table and VSX (type E). Its period is 1.1295241 +- 0.000043 d; the primary eclipse is 1.53 mag deep at phase 0.680 and lasts 0.142 in phase, and the secondary is 0.12 mag deep at phase 0.185. Nothing in the literature or on ExoFOP links that binary to this CTOI. The target itself is not in any EB catalogue.
leads.data_used: QLP SAP for S12, S39, S93 and S104; there are no SPOC or TESS-SPOC light curves. I also did my own TESScut 3x3 photometry and difference imaging for S93 and S104, and used Gaia DR3 neighbours and the Gaia EB parameters. Ephemeris check: the CTOI period error (0.000863 d) makes the catalogue ephemeris useless across sectors; the prediction is off by about 2.6 h, with an uncertainty of about 2 d. When I let the per-sector mid-times be refit freely, the fit wandered off the signal at this S/N, so I fixed the ephemeris from a joint BLS over all four sectors: P = 1.129486 d, T0 = BTJD 1629.95915. The strongest peak within +-0.0025 d lies on the Gaia binary's period (difference 0.7 sigma). Propagating the Gaia primary-eclipse ephemeris (BTJD 446.2149, 1048 cycles) lands on the TESS dips to 4+-67 min. The Gaia secondary would fall half a cycle away. So the TESS dips coincide with the neighbour's primary eclipses.
leads.oddeven: Odd/even agree, as expected, since 1.1295 d is already the binary's true period. QLP SAP, all sectors: odd 1666+-184, even 1575+-146 ppm (0.4 sigma; permutation p = 0.55). Per sector, all within 1.7 sigma. S104 alone: 1513 vs 1501 ppm (0.03 sigma). My TESScut photometry: 614 vs 788 ppm (-1.4 sigma).
leads.secondary: The pipeline's 5.3-sigma secondary does not hold up. Phase 0.5 in QLP, all sectors: 174+-77 ppm (2.3 sigma; 1.75 sigma against the scan). S104 alone: 104+-92 ppm (1.1 sigma). My TESScut photometry: 85+-55 ppm (1.5 sigma). The scan of all phases has nothing beyond |z| = 2.2. A marginal 100-200 ppm dip would match what the Gaia secondary predicts after dilution (about 0.1 of the primary depth in G, and more in the redder TESS band), but in the controls dips at phase 0.5 reach up to 3.1 sigma, so it is not significant here.
leads.other_tests: Depth across sectors: S12 1666+-265, S39 1884+-256, S93 1559+-242 and S104 1508+-215 ppm in QLP SAP; my more contaminated 3x3 aperture gives 692 ppm. Dilution: the neighbour has 0.0025 of the target's TESS flux. The observed ~1600 ppm then requires an intrinsic eclipse of about 0.65 x (1 + contamination), roughly 0.7-0.8 for modest contamination, close to Gaia's primary depth of about 0.76 (1.53 mag) and below 100%, so it is physically consistent. Difference imaging, fitting a PSF from the Gaia scene with free WCS shift and width: in S93 and S104 (different cameras and CCD orientations) the dip source sits on the Gaia binary (offsets 0.08 px and 0.24 px, 2.3 and 1.9 sigma). Putting it on the target is worse by delta-chi2 197 and 29 (offsets 0.55 and 0.65 px, 17 and 5 sigma). The target is RV-quiet in Gaia (error 0.36 km/s over 24 transits). Shape: V-shaped and grazing, and duration (~3 h) matches the Gaia eclipse width; density is not diagnostic.
leads.summary: Nearby eclipsing binary. The CTOI signal is the diluted primary eclipse of TIC 218856692 (Gaia DR3 5952123561802121472, G = 17.87, 10.6" away), a catalogued Gaia/VSX EB. Period (1.12949 vs 1.12952 d), epoch (4+-67 min), depth (required intrinsic ~0.7-0.8 vs Gaia ~0.76) and difference-image location in two sectors all agree, and the target position is rejected. Our pipeline's secondary flag was wrong in significance (not reproduced, under 2.3 sigma), but the candidate is still a false positive for a different, stronger reason. Worth an ExoFOP note naming TIC 218856692 as the source.

leads.already_known: ExoFOP lists it as a PC with no TFOPWG disposition, no observing notes, and it was never made a TOI despite ten sectors. TFOP has SOAR speckle imaging (Ziegler et al. 2020) showing a companion at 0.53" with delta-I = 3.1 (ExoFOP files 2019-07). The ExoFOP CTOI ephemeris is wrong. Its T0 (BJD 2458335.1498) is exactly 1 day off from the paper's Table 2 value (BTJD 1336.1498), and the period 1.4376+-0.0002 is 0.00063 d too short. The ExoFOP ephemeris therefore puts 2026 transits 0.61 d off (0.42 in phase); the paper's T0 is still 4.1 h off. The listed duration (0.88 h) is also wrong; the true duration is about 2.9 h. VSX already has the star as 'KELT KS18C11323', type EA, P = 1.438222 d, with VSX flag 3 (possible duplicate). That catalogue entry is an automated eclipsing-variable label at the same 1.438-d period, so it does not distinguish a planet from an EB. The star is not in Prsa+22, Kostov+25, Gaia EB/NSS, Tey+23 or IJspeert+24. Gaia shows RUWE 2.64 and ipd_frac_multi_peak 72%, consistent with the speckle companion. No follow-up paper flags it as an EB.
leads.data_used: QLP SAP for S1, S2, S28, S29, S68, S69, S95, S96, S103 and S104; TESS-SPOC SAP and PDCSAP for S1, S2, S28, S29, S68 and S69; my own TESScut 3x3 photometry for S103 and S104. Ephemeris check: P = 1.43823063 +- 0.00000021 d (QLP per-sector times, timing residuals 1.3 min or less; per-event fits give 1.4382307), matching KELT's 1.438222. Feinstein's period is 3 sigma off. Our pipeline's 1.4381 came from S104 alone.
leads.oddeven: Even events (relative to T0 = BTJD 3181.4022) are deeper in all 10 QLP sectors and all 6 TESS-SPOC sectors. QLP SAP: odd 14030+-97, even 16700+-161 ppm (14.2 sigma calibrated; permutation z 11.1, p < 2.5e-4; bootstrap 14.0 sigma). The fake-phase null has a spread of 62 ppm, which puts the difference at about 43 sigma. Per sector (QLP, odd/even ppm): S1 14324/17059, S2 14653/16978, S28 14737/18014, S29 14762/18082, S68 14546/18028, S69 14612/18048, S95 13153/14727, S96 13308/14547, S103 13579/16005, S104 12723/15458; each sector is 5.9 to 17.5 sigma. TESS-SPOC PDCSAP: 14277+-67 vs 17252+-69 ppm (31 sigma). My TESScut photometry for S103/S104: 12635+-117 vs 14903+-119 ppm (13.6 sigma). Odd and even durations are equal (2.88 vs 2.92 h) and the timing offset is below 0.3 min, consistent with a circular orbit. The true period is P_EB = 2.8764615 d, with eclipses of about 17250 and 14280 ppm (PDCSAP).
leads.secondary: QLP all sectors, phase 0.5 of 1.438 d: -10+-25 ppm (-0.4 sigma); the phase scan has nothing beyond |z| = 2.6. In my S103/S104 TESScut photometry the same phase gives 209+-60 ppm (3.5 sigma), and QLP S104 alone gives 192+-82 ppm (2.4 sigma). The ten-sector value is zero, and controls reach 3.1 sigma at this phase, so I consider this a systematic. With P_EB = 2P, phase 0.5 of P is quadrature, where no eclipse is expected.
leads.other_tests: Depth across sectors and products: QLP 15.9-16.5k ppm in S1-S69 and 13.8-14.7k ppm in S95-S104, which matches the general QLP suppression in recent sectors seen in the controls. TESS-SPOC PDC gives 15.4-16.1k ppm, steady across sectors. Shape: V-shaped and grazing (b ~1.25); the implied density (0.20 g/cc against TIC 0.44) is degenerate. Host: Gaia is RV-quiet (error 0.89 km/s over 15 transits, amplitude 9.4 km/s), which excludes a near-twin stellar companion around the F star (that would give K ~100 km/s). The EB is therefore most likely on the SOAR companion at 0.53" (flux fraction ~5.5%, needing about a 30% eclipse, which is plausible) or on another unresolved star. Resolved Gaia neighbours add only 0.6% of the target's flux, so none of them can produce a 1.6% dip. Our S104-only rerun gives odd 12777 vs even 15259 ppm (9.4 sigma), reproducing the 12.7-sigma pipeline flag.
leads.summary: The 1.438-d CTOI is an eclipsing binary at P_EB = 2.8764615 d with nearly equal but clearly different eclipses (~17.3k vs ~14.3k ppm PDCSAP). The difference holds in all ten sectors from 2018 to 2026 and in three independent reductions. Gaia RVs exclude the bright F star as the EB host, so the likely host is the known 0.53" companion or another unresolved star. VSX/KELT already labels the star EA at the 1.438-d period, but that does not show it is a binary rather than a planet, and ExoFOP has no false-positive note. ExoFOP's ephemeris is also wrong (T0 typo of 1 day, stale period). Suggested note: P_EB = 2.8764615 d, deeper-eclipse T0 = BJD_TDB 2460181.4022, plus the corrected planet-period ephemeris.

controls:
I ran the identical code on six known or confirmed planets observed in S104 and/or S105, with the same products as the leads (QLP SAP, TESS-SPOC SAP/PDC, SPOC 2-min SAP/PDC). The settings were the same: local quadratic baselines, scatter-calibrated errors, odd/even permutation and bootstrap tests, fake-phase null, and a transit-masked secondary scan. The controls are:
- HIP 65 Ab (TOI-129.01): grazing, P 0.98 d, ~7000 ppm, T = 9.9, 11 sectors including S104/S105.
- WASP-4 b (TOI-232.01): P 1.34 d, 27000 ppm, includes S105.
- WASP-5 b (TOI-250.01): P 1.63 d, 14000 ppm, includes S105.
- WASP-145 Ab (TOI-2206.01): grazing, P 1.77 d, 10000 ppm, includes S104/S105.
- TOI-2193 Ab: P 2.12 d, 8500 ppm, includes S104.
- TOI-2196 b: P 1.19 d, ~950 ppm, includes S104. This is the shallow control for TIC 218856662.

**Odd/even, all sectors.** The calibrated significance was:

| Control | QLP | TESS-SPOC SAP / PDC | SPOC 2-min SAP / PDC |
|---|---|---|---|
| HIP 65 Ab | 0.72 | 0.85 / 0.45 | 1.09 / 0.56 |
| WASP-4 b | -0.06 | -0.80 / -0.43 | -0.09 / 0.04 |
| WASP-5 b | -0.12 | -0.44 / -0.29 | -0.59 / -0.14 |
| WASP-145 Ab | 0.14 | -2.14 / -2.19 (22 events) | -1.32 / -1.00 |
| TOI-2193 Ab | -0.72 | -0.37 / -0.12 | -1.26 / -1.06 |
| TOI-2196 b | -0.21 | -0.02 / -0.32 | 0.37 / 0.39 |

**Odd/even, S104/S105 only.** All controls were within 0.8 sigma: HIP 65 -0.77/-0.25, WASP-4 0.67/0.26, WASP-5 -0.44/0.28, WASP-145 0.64/-0.38, TOI-2193 0.28/-0.45, TOI-2196 0.21/0.48.

**Odd/even, my own TESScut photometry.** HIP 65 -1.25, WASP-4 -1.97.

The largest control value in about 40 measurements is |2.2| sigma. The three odd/even leads sit at 9-31 sigma in multi-sector data and 9-12.5 sigma in S104/S105 alone, with the same sign in every sector. TIC 218856662 is at 0.4 sigma.

**Secondary at phase 0.5.**
- WASP-5 b showed 153+-49 ppm (3.1 sigma), which may be its real occultation.
- WASP-4 b showed 1.9 sigma.
- The other controls were within 1.6 sigma, and none exceeded 0.9 sigma in S104/S105 alone.
- So a 2-3 sigma 'secondary' is not diagnostic. This calibrated the non-significance of TIC 218856662's 2.3-sigma hint.

**Pipeline caveats revealed by the controls.**
1. QLP SAP depths in S94 and later are 10-28% shallower than SPOC PDCSAP for the same planets (for example WASP-4 b S105: 21.1k vs 27.7k ppm; WASP-5 b S105: 10.2k vs 14.2k ppm). Cross-sector depth changes in QLP are therefore not, by themselves, evidence of blending.
2. QLP timestamps in S102-S105 are offset by -3.4 to +3.2 min, with within-sector drifts, relative to SPOC 2-min data, which stay within 0.4 min (HIP 65, WASP-4). QLP-only ephemeris refits in recent sectors carry a few-minute systematic error.
3. For low-S/N targets, letting the per-sector timing refit run freely diverged. This happened for TOI-2196 b and TIC 218856662, and also for TOI-2193 Ab until its stale TOI-catalogue ephemeris was replaced. Those runs used ephemerides fixed from a joint BLS: TOI-2196 b P = 1.194723 d (the TOI-catalogue 1.195397 is stale) and TOI-2193 Ab P = 2.122573 d.

leads.summary:
The target system is an eclipsing binary at P = 1.2973384 d (twice the CTOI period), not a 0.65-d planet.
- **Eclipses:** two V-shaped eclipses (T14 about 1.5 h, T12/T14 about 0.40, the same for both) with depths of about 10.3 and 7.4 ppt in S31 TESS-SPOC. The depth ratio is stable at 0.72-0.80 over 7 years.
- **Depth consistency:** absolute depths differ between sectors and products (S31 about 10.3 ppt in both QLP and TESS-SPOC; S97/S105 QLP about 7.7-8.0 ppt; S4 30-min about 8.7 ppt). This is instrumental dilution and cadence smearing; the shallow/deep ratio stays constant.
- **Source position:** difference images in S31, S97 and S105 put the source 0.7-3.8 arcsec from the target. The diff minus out-of-transit offset is 1.2-2.8 arcsec, against 0.8 and 2.6 arcsec for the WASP-22b and TOI-2421b controls.
- **Neighbours excluded:** the only plausible neighbour is a G = 16.2 M dwarf 29 arcsec away (Gaia DR3 5076118634784852992). It would need eclipses of 34% or more, and the difference images exclude it at 28-105 sigma. It also shows a lower fractional depth in its own pixel than the target pixel does. Every other Gaia star within 126 arcsec either needs more than 100% depth or is excluded at more than 50 sigma.
- **Not the G star itself:** the eclipses need two bodies of similar surface brightness. The G star cannot be one of them, because Gaia sees it as a clean SB1 (123 d, K = 30 km/s, good fit), with no 1.3-d variation of order 100 km/s.
- **Likely configuration:** f(M) = 0.327 Msun, so the unseen companion has M >= 1.2 Msun yet contributes little light. The natural reading is a hierarchical triple: an inner pair of K/M dwarfs (the 1.297-d EB) on a 123-d orbit around the G star. This is an interpretation, not a proof. An eclipse-timing (light-travel-time) test against the Gaia orbit was inconclusive (about 1.4 sigma after calibration). An unresolved background EB within about 2 arcsec cannot be fully excluded with TESS, but it is very unlikely in this sparse field (b = -64 deg).
- **Our search:** the 10.1-sigma odd/even flag is confirmed, but the search depth (5652 ppm from DET_FLUX) is underestimated.
- **Why it is worth reporting:** a strong new result for an observing note; ExoFOP and the literature have nothing comparable. Suggested note: 'Odd/even depths differ by about 27% in S4/S31/S97/S105 (SAP/PDCSAP, local baselines; per-sector z = 7-20, stratified permutation p < 3e-4). The true period is 1.2973384 d (EB with primary/secondary about 10/7.4 ppt in S31, circular, V-shaped). Difference images place the source on the target; the 29-arcsec M dwarf is excluded. Gaia DR3 SB1 (P = 122.9 d, f(M) = 0.33 Msun) suggests a hierarchical triple. Suggest FP/EB.'

judgements.reasons:
I uphold the conclusion, but the investigator overstated the odd/even significance. My code gives about 4.5 sigma combined, not about 6.

(1) Odd/even. SPOC 2-min S27/S67/S68, 155 events, local quadratic baselines and a trapezoid template. Even minus odd is +542 to +565 ppm (5.1-5.3% of the 10.7 ppt depth) in SAP, PDCSAP and TESS-SPOC.
- Significance: permutation within sector 3.9 sigma (p<=1e-4), scatter 4.2, paired adjacent 4.1, fake-ephemeris null 4.15 (1000 random ephemerides, std(z)=1.02).
- Across 7 analysis variants (window, baseline order, template-free box, median) it ranges 3.0-4.8 sigma; the median estimator gives 3.2.
- Injecting a 5% difference at fake phases recovered +502 ppm (expected +533).
- Photon-independent QLP S94-S104 (264 events): +233 to +272 ppm (2.5-2.9%), only 1.7-3.6 sigma depending on estimator (permutation 2.4, paired 2.6). The investigator quoted 3.8.
- Per sector all 8 are positive, but S94 (+48) and S104 (+141) are individually insignificant. 15 of 16 TESS orbits have the same sign.
- Joint relative test: 3.6+-0.8% (4.2-4.7 sigma).
- The pipeline selected this lead in S104 at 2P with a near-equal alternate eclipse, so the SPOC test is a fresh test.

(2) The decisive and most robust argument is the missing occultation. Phase 0.5: +8+-72 ppm (SPOC, quadratic baseline), +22+-43 ppm (QLP S94-S104); combined about +18+-37 ppm, 3-sigma limit about 130 ppm. Any giant planet transiting this 6140 K star at a/R*~1.9 should give >=500-700 ppm (thermal, even with full redistribution), or more if reflective. Gaia RV is constant (amplitude 10 km/s, p=0.28), which also excludes a stellar-mass companion to the F star at 0.39 or 0.78 d.

(3) Caveat on the 'ellipsoidal' term. It is at the CTOI period, cos(2 pi phi_P) = -91 to -123 ppm (3.0-3.8 sigma). That shape is degenerate with a planetary phase curve, so it counts as EB evidence only together with the missing occultation. Harmonics at the 100-ppm level carry systematics: the cos(2 pi phi_2P) term is +84/+96 ppm in SPOC but -118 ppm in QLP.

(4) Shape and host.
- The eclipse is V-shaped (T14 1.39 h, T12 0.65 h); its duration fits a grazing orbit for the F star's density, so shape does not discriminate.
- Difference images (S67, S68, S94, S104) put the source 0.09-0.20 px from the target and reject the G=17.0 star at 33 arcsec (delta-chi2 20-105).
- The G=20.6 Gaia source at 3.3 arcsec would need >100% eclipses.
- So the EB is most likely an unresolved companion (RUWE 2.16) or a close blend; host undetermined.

(5) Controls, identical code. Odd/even |z| <= 1.7 on LHS 3844 b, WASP-4 b, WASP-5 b and HATS-68 b. Note that LHS 3844 b shows -4.9% at -1.7 sigma, so the significance, not the 5% size, is what matters. LHS 3844 b phase harmonics are |z| <= 2.

judgements.reasons:
The stellar-companion (EBLM) conclusion stands, and it rests on the Gaia DR3 SB1, not on the photometry.

- **Conjunction phase:** the Gaia orbit, with the companion in front at nu = 90 deg - omega, predicts a conjunction 0.083 d (phase 0.012) from the TESS transit ephemeris, about 1.5 sigma given the strongly correlated Tperi/omega errors. The opposite convention would be off by half a period.
- **Companion mass:** f(M) = 1.6e-3 Msun gives M2 = 0.127-0.150 Msun for M1 = 1.0-1.3 Msun at i of about 84-90 deg. That is a star, and R2 = k*R* of about 0.16 Rsun fits.
- **Photometry is not diagnostic:** odd/even is null, so our search's 8.4-sigma flag is spurious. A possible occultation at phase 0.5 is +370 +- 62 ppm by per-event scatter, but the fake-phase null gives only z about 3.7 (empirical p = 0.007), and sectors are inconsistent (S95 about 150 ppm). It is tentative, though consistent with the roughly 260 ppm expected for a 3000-K M dwarf.

I could not overturn this: the nearby-EB (NEB) identification is strong and confirmed three independent ways.
1. **Light curves:** the odd/even difference at the CTOI period is enormous and stable. Combined z = 35 (p at the 5e-5 floor); per sector z = 8-20 in SPOC 2-min S3, TESS-SPOC S30 and QLP S30/S97/S104/S105. The pseudo-parity control is null and every control planet has |z| <= 1.3. Only TESS-SPOC S3 at 30-min cadence is insensitive (z = 0.3). At 2P = 0.51289822 d the parities agree (z = -0.1) and the second eclipse sits at phase 0.500 +- 1.2 min.
2. **Difference images:** my own fits in S30, S97, S104 and S105 (two cameras, different orientations) move the source 10.1-14.6" from the target, landing 0.6-4.1" from TIC 100918211 = Gaia DR3 4964530230474371968 (14" at PA 18 deg, G = 15.72, parallax 2.45 vs 6.72 mas, so not comoving). The hypothesis fit prefers it over the target with delta-chi2 = 500-1900 per sector. Controls show offsets of only 0.1-2.5".
3. **Gaia variability:** the Gaia DR3 VEB solution for that star (P = 0.5128965 +- 3e-6 d, 0.6 sigma from TESS) puts its primary eclipse at TESS phase 0.0016 +- 0.003 and its secondary at 0.491 +- 0.014 after propagating 7618 cycles.

**Dilution check:** the neighbour would need about 19% eclipses (diff-image implied 12-17% averaged over both eclipses), consistent with the Gaia G-band depth of 0.27 mag plus ellipsoidal variation. The target's constant Gaia RV and its SOLAR_LIKE/ROT classification support it not being the eclipsing star.

**What is new:** the EB nature at 2P is already published (Prsa+22 lists this TIC at 0.5129265 d, without identifying the source), and Montalto+20 recorded odd/even S/N 5.6 and an unphysical a/R* = 1.18. The source identification is not recorded anywhere: ExoFOP has no notes on the target or on TIC 100918211, Prsa+22 does not flag it, and no paper links the CTOI to the Gaia/VSX EB. The CTOI still reads PC, with Montalto's rank = 1 (on target). A short note crediting Prsa+22 and Gaia DR3 is low-risk and useful.

**Side observation:** the secondary/primary depth ratio drifts from 0.66-0.70 (S3) to 0.54 (S105). This is intrinsic to the EB or systematic, and irrelevant to the conclusion.

judgements.reasons:
I could not overturn it.

Light curves:
(1) Independent BLS gives P=5.13111 d. P/2 gives alternating depths of about 0.5% and 5%, which rules it out. At P, the odd and even primaries are equal. At 2P there is no extra eclipse.
(2) A secondary of 0.55-0.73% (depending on dilution) sits at phase 0.500 in every sector from S12 to S104 and in every product. It has the same about 4 h duration as the primary. Its random-phase-null z is 11-45, with 0/300 fake phases as deep. The all-phase scan peak is at 0.500 (fine scan 0.5000-0.5015), so the orbit is circular. The secondary/primary ratio of about 0.085 is constant across products, so the eclipse is not a dilution or systematics artifact. That ratio implies T2 of about 3500 K. It is about 8x the maximum reflected light.

Host: the S66 2-min difference image peaks on the target pixel for both eclipses (difference/out-of-eclipse = 7.0% and 0.66% there). At the pixels of the bright neighbours (G=9.28 at 93 arcsec, G=9.85 at 123 arcsec, G=11.76 at 106 arcsec) it is at most 0.1%. SPOC DV gives a TIC offset of 0.27 arcsec (0.11 sigma). All Gaia stars within 60 arcsec are at least 4.6 mag fainter.

Gaia: the DR3 SB1 orbit of this source (P=5.130389+-0.00042 d, 1.8 sigma from TESS; K1=38.78 km/s) gives f(M)=0.0309 Msun, so M2 is about 0.44-0.49 Msun. Its 'primary behind' conjunction falls 0.02 d (MC +-0.38 d) from the observed primary eclipse. The other assignment would be about 2.5 d off.

Novelty (the investigator missed some of this): SPOC S66 DV, public since 2023, already detected the secondary (TCE 1 secondary depth 6553+-263 ppm at 2.562 d; TCE 2 at P=5.13076 d is the secondary at phase 0.5005). ExoMiner++ (Valizadegan+2025, AJ 170, 287, table13) labels both TCEs FP; they are unmatched to the CTOI and no EB statement is made. On ExoFOP the CTOI is still PC since 2021, with 0 observing notes, no TFOP data and no TOI. SIMBAD has only the Gaia SB1 entry. It is absent from VSX, Gaia VEB, ASAS-SN, Prsa+22, Kostov+25 and Tey+23. No paper calls this CTOI an EB. A note is therefore new and useful as a consolidation and correction. It should cite the SPOC, ExoMiner++ and Gaia results rather than claim a discovery.
